A recruiter reaches out. They tell you you’re a good candidate for a senior role or board seat. The opportunity is plausible, but edging into the too-good-to-be-true zone. That’s exactly what happened over a year ago to an operations executive who contacted me. I’m an executive and board résumé writer. They wrote: “I want to confirm you’re the person I’ve…
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: AI Is Changing What We Learn. Is L&D Changing Fast Enough?
item.description:
AI is reshaping learning and development (L&D) by requiring new skills and critical thinking. This shift demands an update in how organizations allocate development time and track competencies. Note: insights from a single organization may not capture your specific L&D needs.
— via HRD Connect

item.title: Free Employment Verification Letter Template and 7 Samples
item.description:
AIHR provides a free employment verification letter template. It standardizes how companies verify employment for landlords, lenders, or immigration authorities. The limitation: it's a template, so it might need tweaking for specific legal or cultural contexts.
— via AIHR

item.title: What Top Performers Do Differently with AI—and Why They See the Biggest Benefits
item.description:
Top performers use AI differently and get more benefits, says HBR. This suggests evaluating how AI is integrated into workflows can boost productivity. Remember, it's based on premium HBR research, so access may be limited.
— via HBR

item.title: What AI is making scarce and why HR should care
item.description:
HR Zone discusses AI's impact on workforce productivity and intelligence abundance. The key question is how to use newfound intelligence instead of just automating. The catch: insights from this may chiefly apply to knowledge-driven roles.
— via HRZone

item.title: This advice from Tom Hanks changed how I work
item.description:
I was writing a book about the perils of recklessly chasing new things when I had an idea: I should interview Tom Hanks. I had read about how Hanks was an avid typewriter collector, and the typewriter seemed like the perfect foil to today’s futuristic gizmos. It’s heavy and impractical. It has no connection to the internet, no delete key, no spell check.… It landed in the last few hours.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Is an HR Generalist Certification Worth It? How to Decide for Your Career
item.description:
Is an HR Generalist certification worth it? For many early- and mid-career HR professionals, it is, as long as you choose a certification that matches your goal. The right one can show employers you understand the full HR cycle, from hiring and onboarding to payroll and policy. Still, it won’t replace proof that you can… The post Is an HR Generalist…
— via AIHR

item.title: Shapers and Founders: Understanding the owner mindset
item.description:
Marrying Eastern philosophy and Western management culture has given many of Asia’s owner-CEOs a unique edge in growing their businesses.
— via McKinsey

item.title: Auditing AI-Washing in German Startups: A Mixed-Methods Study of Marketing Claims and Perceptions
item.description:
AI-washing is the use of 'AI' as a marketing term where products' claims are exaggerated, likely to capture the hype from investors and consumers. In this paper, we examine how startups market AI and how people perceive those claims. We audited the German startup market, applying an annotation codebook of seven dimensions to 100 startups and conducting 63…
— via arXiv

item.title: Dhanashree Raaj to lead global people strategy at Prodevans Technologies, as CHRO
item.description:
Dhanashree Raaj has joined Prodevans Technologies as chief human resources officer (CHRO), taking responsibility for the company’s global people strategy as it looks to scale its operations, strengthen leadership capabilities and build a high-performing, people-centric culture. Raaj brings more than two decades of HR leadership experience across technology,… It landed in the last few hours.
— via HR Katha

item.title: As companies spend more on AI, many spend less on workers
item.description:
Companies are spending more on AI, sometimes at the expense of their workforce. A study found AI was the main reason behind over 120,000 job cuts this year. The issue? The data mostly comes from the tech sector and might not reflect other industries as closely.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: What every HR leader should ask themselves about their wellbeing
item.description:
An article urges HR leaders to focus on their wellbeing as World Mental Health Day nears. It emphasizes the importance of self-care to keep up with HR's demanding role. The perspective is from one author, and your mileage may vary depending on personal circumstances.
— via HRZone

item.title: Republicans, Democrats alike more bullish on DEI in 2026
item.description:
Bipartisan support for DEI in workplaces is on the rise per a Gallup poll. This shift could mean more integrated DEI strategies across industries. However, public opinion can change, and implementation practices remain inconsistent.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Supreme Court sidesteps employment law cases on disability bias, vaccines
item.description:
The Supreme Court is avoiding key employment law cases right now. This leaves business leaders without clear guidance on issues like disability bias and vaccines. It's a reminder to stay up-to-date with appeals court decisions on these topics.
— via HR Dive

item.title: AI adoption may be hampering future organizational growth
item.description:
AI adoption could stall organizational growth if not paired with employee development. A report finds many positions are changed but lack a related opportunity for growth. Coverage is broad and might oversimplify complex organizational dynamics.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Download - Redesigning work for the AI era
item.description:
A new guide suggests ways to redesign work in the age of AI. It offers principles for rethinking jobs and team structures to keep up with technological changes. But remember, it's a one-size-fits-all playbook; individual company needs can vary.
— via Charter

item.title: The 6 Essential Skills Your Workforce Needs to Keep Pace with AI
item.description:
HBR lists six skills employees need to keep pace with AI developments. Skills like adaptability and data literacy help future-proof the workforce. The catch: this is a broad list and might not fit each organization's unique needs.
— via HBR

item.title: When Compliance Workarounds Backfire
item.description:
A piece warns that compliance workarounds can backfire. Using Glovo's legal challenges in Spain as a case study, it shows risks of sidestepping laws. But the discussion stays focused on a single company's experience and may not map onto other sectors.
— via MIT Sloan

item.title: Why your boss matters more than remote or hybrid work when it comes to burnout and job satisfaction
item.description:
Research indicates that a good manager weighs more on job satisfaction than work location. Feeling valued and appreciated by a boss beats out remote or hybrid perks. Keep in mind, the findings rely on existing data and might overlook emerging nuances.
— via The Conversation Business

item.title: AI-Driven Urge Regulation Assistant (AURA): Designing Preemptive Smart Wearables for Smoking Cessation
item.description:
Researchers are designing AI wearables to help quit smoking before cravings hit. These gadgets could proactively support user autonomy in managing habits. This idea is still in the pilot stage and based on interviews with only 10 people.
— via arXiv

item.title: Using production rates to excel at executing construction projects
item.description:
McKinsey suggests using production rates to improve construction outcomes. By achieving small, specific targets, companies can boost productivity. The insight is great for construction, but might not be as applicable to different industries.
— via McKinsey

item.title: 21+ HR Rules and Regulations Your HR Team Needs To Know
item.description:
HR needs to keep up with key rules and regulations across industries. Overlooking these can lead to serious legal and reputational consequences. The list may feel overwhelming, but not all rules apply to every sector.
— via AIHR

item.title: Young workers are turning toward AI-proof jobs
item.description:
Young workers are seeking jobs less likely to be automated by AI. As many degree-required positions become scarce, they're looking to fields needing human touch. These job shifts reflect only early trends and might adjust as tech evolves.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Jyothsana Vasudevan takes charge of people agenda at SRF, as president and CHRO
item.description:
Jyothsana Vasudevan is now leading HR at SRF as president and CHRO. With over 24 years in HR leadership, she brings a wealth of experience. It’s a big move for SRF, but applies to just one company — watch for similar shifts elsewhere.
— via HR Katha

item.title: Coworkers say they distrust each other more than ever
item.description:
A survey shows distrust among coworkers is now at a record high. This erosion of trust impacts collaboration and productivity. It's widespread data with 34,000 respondents, but remember it’s one survey over two years.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Long onboarding times can cause cybersecurity skill decay
item.description:
HR Dive warns that lengthy onboarding can harm cybersecurity skills. Fast onboarding could preserve these vital abilities. This is vendor-researched, so take it as an advisory, not a definitive stance.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Top HR conferences for 2027
item.description:
HR Dive lists key HR conferences for 2027. Planning ahead with these dates can enrich training and talent acquisition strategies. It's promotional, aimed at those planning their conference calendar.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Miami furniture store will pay $1.3M to settle charge it favored Hispanic applicants
item.description:
A Miami furniture store settles a discrimination charge for $1.3M. It's a reminder that compliance in hiring practices is crucial. It happened in the US and may not directly compare to other contexts.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Research: Sleep Deprivation Is a Leadership Problem
item.description:
A new study says sleep deprivation is a leadership problem. Leaders not getting enough rest may make poor decisions, affecting teams and company performance. The catch: the article relies on premium research, so access might be restricted.
— via HBR

item.title: Beyond Barbie and Ken: How unconscious gender bias still shapes the boardroom
item.description:
An article highlights how unconscious gender bias still affects boardrooms. Recognizing and tackling these biases could improve gender fairness and team dynamics. It's based on one write-up of ongoing issues, so it's more of a conversation starter than a solution.
— via HRZone

item.title: The Real Reasons Why Digital Projects Fail
item.description:
MIT Sloan explores why digital projects often fail. Employees say many tools add more inefficiency than they solve. It's primarily opinion-based with no hard numbers, so take it as managerial insight rather than proof.
— via MIT Sloan

item.title: The Infrastructure Opportunities Hiding in Plain Sight with NOVA Infrastructure’s Allison Kingsley and Chris Beall
item.description:
NOVA Infrastructure's work is deeper than it looks, says Bain. They highlight untapped opportunities within existing systems that firms might ignore. It’s an interview format, so heavy on opinions and less empirical evidence.
— via Bain

item.title: Ownership and Non-Neutral Technological Change: Evidence from China's State-Owned Enterprise Privatization
item.description:
A new paper examines China’s SOE privatization impact on productivity. It shows short-term gains in labor productivity which fade over time. It's very specific to the Chinese context and historical data, so broader applicability is limited.
— via arXiv

item.title: Understanding Interfirm AI Talent Flow Networks through Online Professional Profiles
item.description:
Researchers analyze how AI talent flows across companies. The study tracks how firms gain or lose AI skills, revealing competitive patterns. It's a dense academic work mainly relevant to larger organizations dealing with AI.
— via arXiv

item.title: Organizational Lifespan as Commitment: The Case of Foundations
item.description:
A report looks at organizational commitment through foundations' lifespan planning. It shows how foundation choices can influence long-term planning and continuity. Niche focus means it's more applicable to philanthropic or nonprofit entities.
— via arXiv

item.title: HR Annual Calendar 2027: Key Dates and Free Template
item.description:
AIHR offers a free HR annual calendar template. This helps HR leaders plot out important dates and meet compliance and management goals. Standard calendar advice, useful if you're looking for structure.
— via AIHR

item.title: Two-thirds of workers use DIY ‘hacks’ to make office life more bearable
item.description:
A survey finds two-thirds of workers are personalizing office spaces secretly. DIY hacks signal unmet needs for comfort and personalization at work. It's from a single survey, covering a slice of office workers.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: From Syngene to T-Hub: Somesh Ganti appointed director – HR
item.description:
Somesh Ganti's move to director-HR at T-Hub underlines leadership trends in start-ups. HR transitions like this indicate the growing importance of agile HR roles. It's an individual appointment, so reflective more of T-Hub’s direction than industry-wide.
— via HR Katha

item.title: Employee Xperience Expo 2026 NORTH: Leadership, wellbeing and inclusion take centre stage
item.description:
The Employee Xperience Expo is highlighting employee experience, inclusion, and engagement. It's a chance to learn new strategies for a more inclusive workplace on November 10th in Manchester. Catch: It's an event preview—actual insights will depend on the sessions attended.
— via HRZone

item.title: The fragmented leader is finished: A new path to whole leadership
item.description:
A piece argues the 'fragmented leader' is out, proposing 'Whole Leadership' instead. The focus on aligning leadership skills to build trust might help in improving employee relations. Catch: These are philosophical ideas worth exploring but not ready-made solutions.
— via HRZone

item.title: How to get a job in this ‘low-hire, low-fire’ market
item.description:
Fast Company describes how hard it is to get a job in a ‘low-hire, low-fire’ market. This means companies might struggle to find the right talent amidst high application volumes. Catch: Most insights come from a single staffing agency's experience in LA.
— via Fast Company Work Life

item.title: Transgender former EEOC employee may proceed with bias lawsuit, judge says
item.description:
A former EEOC employee can proceed with a bias lawsuit for a hostile work environment. This underscores the importance of maintaining an unbiased and inclusive workplace culture. Catch: Details are specific to this case, so apply lessons carefully.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Settled: 7 lawsuits employers resolved in September
item.description:
HR Dive lists seven resolved lawsuits revealing challenges with DEI initiatives. Takeaway: Ensure DEI programs are fair and don't inadvertently discriminate. Catch: These cases are resolved and context-specific, so use them as reference points, not templates.
— via HR Dive

item.title: Strategic intellectual property management may maximize government’s return on investment
item.description:
Deloitte's study suggests the government might boost returns by smartly managing its intellectual property. For HR leaders, this emphasizes how strategic asset management can lead to better financial outcomes. Catch: This is based on governmental examples—businesses will need customized strategies.
— via Deloitte

item.title: Your Sales Team Has a New Workforce
item.description:
Gartner notes a shift in the make-up of sales teams with a new workforce composition affecting performance. For HR, this may mean reviewing sales roles and competencies for current relevance. Catch: Specific details on what changes entail are sparse in this brief.
— via Gartner

item.title: TrustmeWatcher: An Application for Workplace Micro-Sensing and Explainable Well-Being Feedback
item.description:
TrustmeWatcher aims to sync behavior data and feedback for better well-being insights at work. This tool shows potential for more accurate employee experience analysis. Catch: It's still in the early stages, and practical deployment details are limited.
— via arXiv

item.title: AI’s Impact on Financial Services
item.description:
A post from Wharton highlights AI's growing impact on financial services. This could mean big productivity gains and innovation for HR in finance roles. Catch: The piece broadly covers AI—specific actionable steps for HR still need fleshing out.
— via Knowledge at Wharton

item.title: Asymmetric Information in Wage Contracts: Experimental Evidence and Welfare Implications
item.description:
A study reveals challenges of fixed wages in productivity and adverse selection. HR folks can take this data on wage structures for reviewing compensation strategies. Catch: The research is experimental and contextually tied to specific wage structures.
— via arXiv

item.title: Synthetic Cultural Agents from Aggregate Anchors
item.description:
Research introduces synthetic cultural agents for better group preference profiling. HR can potentially use similar models for training or employee analysis. Catch: The paper's application in everyday HR functions is theoretical at this point.
— via arXiv
